speaker: Doctor
text: Let me start by understanding the timeline and nature of your symptoms. You mentioned difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, and speech difficulties; when did these symptoms first appear, and have they worsened gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. To better localize the issue, does the incontinence present as urgency or retention, and do you notice any numbness in your legs or hands? Also, have you experienced any sudden onset of weakness or double vision?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive difficulty walking. I also have Urinary incontinence, Slurred speech, Rigidity in limbs, Mild hand tremor, Orthostatic hypotension. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Cellulitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spinal Cord Compression (likely due to a tumor or severe degenerative myelopathy). The patient's symptoms of progressive gait difficulty, urinary incontinence, slurred speech (dysarthria), limb rigidity, and orthostatic hypotension are classic signs of spinal cord pathology affecting the cervical region, not cellulitis. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Cervical Spine.
